penalties.authority: Office of the Assistant Commissioner of State Tax, Ahmedabad
penalties.details: Office of the Assistant Commissioner of State Tax, Ahmedabad by an order dated 24th December, 2025 has raised demand of tax of ₹ 4,26,789 under Section 73 of the Gujarat Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 read with the corresponding provisions of Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 and Integrated Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 alleging discrepancies in the disclosures in the GST Annual Return for FY 2021-22 w.r.t Input Tax Credit claimed in FY 2022-23, along with interest of ₹3,21,180 and a penalty of ₹42,679.
penalties.impact: There is no material impact on financials, operations or other activities of the Company. The Company is in the process of filing an appeal against the said Order.

penalties.authority: Office of the Deputy Commissioner of State Tax, Enforcement, Division - 7, Surat
penalties.details: Office of the Deputy Commissioner of State Tax, Enforcement, Division - 7, Surat, had by an order dated 20th January, 2026 raised demand of fine and penalty of ₹ 8,34,886 under section section 130 of The Gujarat Goods and Service Tax Act read with the corresponding section 130 of the Central Goods and Service Tax Act / Section 21 of the Union Territory Goods and Service Tax Act or Under section 20 of the Integrated Goods and Service Tax Act alleging movement of goods without valid documents like tax invoice, credit note, any return challan and non generation of E way bill.

tax_litigation.as_last_disclosed: The matter pertains to a service tax demand of ₹22,64,694/- (along with an equivalent penalty) raised by Commissioner of Central Excise, Customs and Service Tax, Cochin alleging non-inclusion of certain charges in the taxable value and availment of certain incorrect deductions for the period from July 2003 to December 2005. This was pending in appeal (filed by the Company) before Custom, Excise & Service Tax Appellate Tribunal (CESTAT), Bangalore and the same was reported to the Stock Exchanges vide its letter dated 14th August, 2023 along with other pending material litigations / disputes in line with the requirements of Regulation 30 of the LODR Regulations, 2015 read with Schedule III and relevant SEBI Circular thereunder.
tax_litigation.opposing_party: Commissioner of Central Excise, Customs and Service Tax Appeals, Cochin
tax_litigation.status: Based on the Order of CESTAT received by the Company during the quarter, the matter has been decided in favor of the Company, and the service tax demand and penalty thereof has been dropped.

tax_litigation.as_last_disclosed: The matter pertains to an excise demand of ₹1,59,228/- along with an equivalent penalty raised by Commissioner of Central Excise, Customs Adjudication – Vapi alleging wrongful availment of Cenvat Credit by Universal Comfort Products Limited (UCPL) which got merged with the Company during the financial year 2020-21. This was pending in appeal (filed by the Company) before Custom, Excise & Service Tax Appellate Tribunal (CESTAT), Ahmedabad and the same was reported to the Stock Exchanges vide its letter dated 14th August, 2023 along with other pending material litigations / disputes in line with the requirements of Regulation 30 of the LODR Regulations, 2015 read with Schedule III and relevant SEBI Circular thereunder.
tax_litigation.opposing_party: Customs, Excise & Service Tax Appellate Tribunal West Zonal Bench at Ahemdabad
tax_litigation.status: Based on the Order of CESTAT received by the Company during the quarter, the matter has been decided in favor of the Company, and the excise demand and penalty thereof has been dropped.

timeline.summary: Voltas' Q4 FY26 call (14 May 2026) reported FY26 PAT at ₹377 Cr and UCP margin at 3.2%; with management guiding only a gradual margin recovery.

Voltas held Q1FY27 earnings conference call on 14 August 2026, reporting 18.6% YoY revenue growth to ₹4,765 Cr and announcing a binding term sheet for a 50-50 JV with Atomberg to manufacture RAC compressors in India.

watchlist.text: UCP segment margin recovery toward FY25 level

watchlist.response: Management said recovery would be gradual and declined to give a timeline, citing demand and commodity volatility.
watchlist.text: Analysts pressed on the path of UCP margins from 3.2% in FY26 back to FY25's 8.4%, and on whether FY25 profitability is achievable in FY27.

watchlist.response: CFO said marketing was within the normal pool and did not quantify the forex loss beyond noting it hit unallocated costs.
watchlist.text: Analysts asked for quantification of the forex loss (around ₹55 Cr in H2) and the incremental marketing spend on brand ambassadors.

watchlist.response: Management gave the rounds taken (5% 3-star, 10% 5-star, 2-3% copper) but said the next round depends on war and rupee movement, without a number.
watchlist.text: Analysts asked how much of the double-digit commodity inflation has been passed through and what further price hikes are planned.
Satisfactory due diligence, product validation, definitive agreements and necessary approvals for Atomberg JV

watchlist.response: Management acknowledged margin pressure but expects gradual improvement over next 8 quarters through scale, cost optimization, and better absorption of fixed costs
watchlist.text: Achieving sustainable 7-8% UCP EBITDA margin given current pressures

watchlist.response: Confirmed breakeven pushed back by few quarters due to commodity price increases that couldn't be fully passed to market
watchlist.text: Voltbek EBITDA breakeven timeline delayed due to West Asia crisis
